text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Swedish companies have this year bought U.S. companies for almost 24 billion crowns, according to a survey. In the latest deal, Forcenergy is to pay 1.3 billion crowns for U.S. oil and gas companies Edisto Resources Corp and Convest Energy. Swedish companies say they are branching out into new markets in Asia but they are also continuing to establish markets in the U.S. and Europe. So far this year about 70 Swedish companies have bought companies overseas, which could set a new record, according to Magnus Heinsted of Acquisitions and Mergers. In 1996, 135 companies bought overseas.
- The Stockholm bourse is continuing to see relatively high activity with the general index rising to a new high on Monday in fairly good trade of 5.8 billion crowns.
- Car drivers caught drink-driving cannot drive a car but they can still fly a plane, according to aviation commission rules.

- Swedish/U.S. drugs company Pharmacia & Upjohn can benefit from the shake out in the tobacco industry in the U.S. with its Nicorette products that are designed to help people give up smoking. Sales in the U.S. last year hit about $300 million but income from Nicorette in the U.S. slipped in the first quarter of 1997 by 40 percent to $13 million.

- Shares in Swedish drug company Astra are nearing a new record amid market expectations of imminent U.S. approval for asthma treatment, the Pulmicort Turbuhaler, and with positive market sentiment about the company after a mini-roadshow in Britain last week.

- Vehicle maker Volvo sacked the managing director of its German subsidiary, Svante Runnquist, by mistake, said the paper, quoting an internal company investigation as its source. Runnquist was sacked 18 months ago together with the company's two leading salesmen, accused of fraud.
- Sweden's leading brokerage, Alfred Berg, has in a short time lost over 20 of the key people in the market. The moves came after the company paid out bonuses of about 200 million crowns.

- Market players are becoming more optimistic about economic growth in Sweden this year, according to a survey by the paper. Most expect to see growth of two percent this year and about three percent next year.
